note: Proof that vLLM can serve as the teacher for the next healing data (written 2026-11-04, before any run). The user approved the plan (generate with the dense 9B in vLLM, keep correct answers, prefer short ones, store the teacher's top-k log-probs, heal in time-boxed local and pod sessions) and added: 'we have to prove the vllm as well'. Three things must hold before any data is generated for training: vLLM's 9B answers as well as our HF dense model does; the log-probs it returns are the ones our HF teacher would give for the same tokens (the healing loss would use them in place of a teacher pass); and its speed is what the cost estimates assumed. One pod, no training.
model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B at the pinned revision of every earlier pod (run_slim_pod.MODEL), bf16.

vllm.settings: LLM(dtype bfloat16, max_model_len 8192, logprobs_mode raw_logprobs, max_logprobs 20, generation_config 'vllm', no images or video). The returned log-probs must be the model's own (raw, before temperature, penalties or top-k/top-p), which is what a teacher pass gives.
vllm.environment: Its own virtual environment (vLLM pins torch 2.14.0 and transformers >= 5.16.1); the comparison runs in the bundle's usual environment (torch 2.14.1, transformers 5.14.1), the one healing uses.

parts.check: The 96 GSM8K check prompts (probe_prompts_96.json) with thinking on and with thinking off, each sampled once with the model card's settings (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, presence penalty 1.5; seed 26103103 + prompt index), cap 4,096, top-20 log-probs kept.
parts.throughput: Train problems (vllm_proof_problems.jsonl: GSM8K train rows the corpus does not use, and MATH train), 4 samples each, thinking on, the same sampler and cap, in batches until 40 minutes have passed: generated tokens per second over the whole time, and the share answered correctly.
parts.fidelity: 32 of the thinking-on check answers (the first 32 that finished), teacher-forced through the bundle's HF Qwen3.5-9B in bf16 (as healing's teacher runs): per generated position, the HF log-probability of the sampled token and of vLLM's top-20 tokens.

predictions.accuracy: Thinking on, vLLM gets 64 to 82 of 96 right (HF dense 9B: 73, 78 finished, in section 18's pod check); thinking off, within 9 of dense_check's local HF figure if that has finished (else reported only).
predictions.logprobs: Over all fidelity positions: the sampled token's log-probability differs from HF's by under 0.05 nats on average and under 0.5 at the 99th percentile; vLLM's top-1 token is HF's top-1 at 97% or more of positions; the KL between the two distributions renormalized over vLLM's top 20 averages under 0.02 nats.
predictions.throughput: At least 1,000 generated tokens per second on the pod's 48 GB card (the cost estimates assumed 1,500 to 3,000 on faster cards); under 1,000 means the generation estimates were too low and are redone before any shard is bought.
predictions.vocab: Under 1% of vLLM's top-20 probability mass falls on tokens outside the student's 64K vocabulary (reported; the healing loss renormalizes over the kept rows).

pass: vLLM is used for teacher data only if accuracy and logprobs hold. If logprobs fails, generation may still use vLLM, but the healing teacher pass stays in HF.
budget: A $5 cap (runpod_budget_vllm_proof_20261104.json), one 48 GB card at most $0.60/h, 3-hour deadline.
